title: Starmer Fights for Survival in Make-or-Break Speech
excerpt: After Labour's worst local election in decades, the UK PM faces 40+ MPs demanding his resignation — and delivers a defiant reset address.
body:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer delivered a politically charged address on Monday, May 11, vowing to 'face up to the big challenges' as he fought off a growing rebellion inside his own Labour Party.

**What happened — a party in open revolt:**
Labour lost more than 1,400 council seats and control of 37 councils in last week's local elections, triggering immediate calls for Starmer's departure. As of Sunday evening, 42 Labour MPs were publicly demanding his resignation. Former Deputy Prime Minister Angela Rayner declared that 'what we are doing isn't working, and it needs to change,' while MP Catherine West told the BBC she was actively collecting colleagues' names to force a formal leadership timetable.

**What Starmer pledged — a harder, faster reset:**
In his speech, Starmer cited growth, national defence, energy, and Europe as the battlegrounds that will define his government. He pledged to put Britain 'at the heart of Europe,' targeting a youth mobility deal with the EU and closer trade ties. He also committed to nationalising British Steel and said he would not 'walk away' from any leadership challenge. Health Secretary Wes Streeting and ex-Deputy PM Rayner are already being named as potential successors, with Bloomberg reporting that 'several would-be contenders are sitting on the sidelines.'

**What to watch — markets and King's Speech:**
UK gilt yields rose after the speech as West renewed her push for a leadership contest; Starmer's ability to survive until Wednesday's King's Speech — which sets out his legislative agenda — will be the next critical test of whether this reset holds.
